video_title: Is Bitcoin About to Shock Everyone in Q4?
gist: Jordi Visser tells Anthony Pompliano that macro doom over rising rates is misplaced because the economy is now AI/tech-dominated (56% of S&P) and rate-insensitive, while they debate whether OpenAI/Anthropic face per-customer token leakage or a compute-driven re-acceleration. Visser argues personal AI agents require instant crypto settlement, sees Q4 institutional allocation and a 'Micron moment' in token volumes (his 46-name index +50% YTD vs Bitcoin -3.2%), and Pompliano flags regulation as the brake on agentic investing.

themes.theme: Macro doom is wrong: rates normalized, economy restructured

insights.claim: Jordi Visser calls the current macro fear over rising rates, $100 oil and a higher 10-year 'stupid', arguing it is just another item on the list of doomer narratives like tariffs and war.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Visser stays risk-on despite consensus macro fear from traditional investors.
insights.quote: I actually think it's stupid. Podcast over.

insights.claim: Visser argues rates at '20-year highs' have merely normalized after being held at zero post-GFC, and with nominal GDP at roughly 6.5%, a 10-year yield at or below nominal GDP is still cheap.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Rate level relative to nominal growth, not absolute level, is what matters for equities.
insights.quote: So really what's happened to rates is they've normalized. Nominal GDP is six and change percent.

insights.claim: Visser says rates mattered greatly before the GFC because the economy was built on autos and housing, but post-2007 (the iPhone era) the economy is structurally different so historical 50-year analogs no longer apply.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Discount macro signals calibrated on the old autos/housing economy.
insights.quote: it's not the same economy as before 2007. And that's because of the iPhone.

insights.claim: In 2015 Ford, GM and the homebuilders had nearly 20x the annual revenue of Micron and Nvidia; today Micron and Nvidia alone exceed them combined, and Nvidia's expected next-year revenue growth is almost the size of that entire group's revenue.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Capital should keep rotating from static sectors into accelerating AI hardware.

insights.claim: Visser believes homebuilders will struggle 'forever' because younger generations prefer mobility over the buy-a-house-and-stay-30-years model, favoring apartments and Airbnb-style housing instead.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Structural short/underweight thesis on homebuilders independent of rates.
insights.quote: I think home builders are going to have a tough time for ever.

insights.claim: Technology including tech-like names in other sectors (Netflix, Google, Meta, Amazon, Tesla) is now about 56% of the S&P 500, versus roughly 13% when the iPhone launched.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Index-level behavior is now dominated by AI/tech, not rate-sensitive sectors.
insights.quote: You're up to 56% of the S&P 500 now.

insights.claim: Visser argues poor market breadth and 52-week lows are concentrated in rate-sensitive consumer staples, utilities and real estate, which act as synthetic bond positions hurt by AI-driven higher rates, so bad breadth is by definition rather than a crash signal.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Avoid bond-proxy sectors while rates rise; don't read bad breadth as a top.
insights.quote: who wants to own a consumer staples and a utility when they're basically just synthetic bond positions when bond rates are going higher?

insights.claim: Visser claims the AI trade has no sensitivity to interest rates, citing Micron's 87% margins reported this week and the pricing power of Anthropic and OpenAI selling scarce compute.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Rising rates are not a reason to sell AI hardware/compute names.
insights.quote: there is absolutely no sensitivity for rates in the AI trade. None.

insights.claim: Visser sees a near-term rate relief setup: David Zervos brought into Treasury to lower long-term rates, another Treasury buyback/curve twist, lower-than-expected core PCE, and weaker unemployment and hourly earnings data; rates just need to stop rising daily.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Stabilizing long rates into midterms and earnings season is bullish for risk assets.
insights.quote: They don't have to go down, guys. They just need to not be a story where every day they go up.

themes.theme: Model labs debate: OpenAI/Anthropic growth vs. leakage

insights.claim: Pompliano has turned more cautious on Anthropic and OpenAI, citing falling token consumption per customer (Ramp AI index spend down, OpenRouter-type metrics), falling token prices, and Anthropic revenue appearing to plateau, since tokens times price equals lab revenue.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Value in AI may reallocate away from model labs even as the broad AI trade continues.
insights.quote: there's an increasing chance that they are going to be way underperform what people think

insights.claim: Pompliano argues OpenAI and Anthropic are an on-ramp: customers start there, then optimize by building cheaper/better intelligence in-house, so labs must keep onboarding non-AI users to replace leaking per-customer usage; Sylvia claims a <10-engineer team beats them for personal finance.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Expect enterprise in-sourcing to pressure lab per-customer revenue.
insights.quote: I think that open anthropic for many businesses are the perfect on-ramp

insights.claim: Visser says the early-year 'token maxing' phase of inefficient token use was always going to end, token costs are deflationary, and the ensuing agentic phase will make token numbers explode.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Recent token-usage dip is an air pocket, not a trend reversal.
insights.quote: the first part of this year was about token maxing.

insights.claim: Visser says OpenAI and Anthropic's combined revenue this year will exceed total software revenue, Anthropic went from a $50B to multi-trillion valuation in a year and a half with a 100B+ annualized run rate, yet he does not expect them to reach $1 trillion in revenue and believes their fastest growth is past.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Don't fade the labs, but growth rate deceleration is already underway.
insights.quote: Anthropic was a $50 billion company. It's now a multi-t trillion in a year and a half.

insights.claim: Visser argues frontier users like biotech, nanotech, physical sciences, and hedge funds such as Jane Street and Millennium (already on Anthropic) will pay for frontier intelligence rather than cheaper models, and that Gemini and open-source models make mistakes Claude and OpenAI fix.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: High-stakes use cases sustain premium pricing for top labs.
insights.quote: You're crazy if you think they're going to use cheaper models.

insights.claim: Visser warns the next year is a 'very dangerous period' because AI usage will skyrocket (Jevons paradox, only ~1% of usage today) and there isn't enough compute.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Compute scarcity favors owners of compute and chip suppliers.
insights.quote: The usage is going to skyrocket and we don't have enough compute.

insights.claim: Citing SemiAnalysis and All-In speculation, the speakers note OpenAI and Anthropic combined may own up to 50% of new compute coming online, including Vera Rubin chips, which Visser says could re-accelerate their growth next year.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Compute ownership as a moat could reverse the lab-deceleration narrative.
insights.quote: open anthropic combined will own up to 50% of all the compute coming online

insights.claim: Visser argues agent swarms make slow legacy settlement (weekend wires, multi-step card flows) a security risk, since every extra second is an opening for theft, so instant cryptographic settlement is a necessity and Visa and Mastercard 'have no chance' as agent-commerce winners.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Bearish on card networks, bullish on crypto settlement rails for agent payments.
insights.quote: Well, Vis and Mastercard are going to be the winners in this." I'm like, "No, they're not. They have no chance.

insights.claim: Visser says crypto didn't need the altcoins and tokens; layer-1s were needed to draw capital to build infrastructure, and agents are now the 'app store moment' use case, as Uber only emerged after the App Store.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Favor L1 ecosystems as infrastructure for agentic commerce.

themes.theme: Q4 crypto bull setup and institutional demand

insights.claim: Visser says Bitcoin moving above 82,000 confirmed the bull trend, fundamentals are strengthening daily, and FOMO is about to kick in, driven by new players entering.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Bullish on crypto into year-end.
insights.quote: I said before when Bitcoin got above 82,000, that was the confirmation of the bull trend.

insights.claim: Visser reports hedge funds and asset managers (three calls this week) are proactively asking why to invest in crypto, a reversal from when the door had to be pried open; banks like Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Citi are racing on tokenization and stablecoins.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Institutional demand is building ahead of allocation decisions.

insights.claim: Visser argues large allocators make next-year decisions in Q4, especially the final two months as performance pay crystallizes, but their crypto options are limited to ETFs, DATs and about five public stocks, creating an underlying bid for L1s while alt beta stays retail-driven until tokenization.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Q4 allocation season supports crypto; tokenization unlocks institutional alt flows.

insights.claim: Visser's equal-weight 46-name crypto ecosystem index (L1s and L2s, 42 tokens plus 4 public stocks) is up 50% year-to-date while Bitcoin is down 3.2%, reversing the prior period when Bitcoin led and alts lagged.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Broad ecosystem exposure is outperforming Bitcoin in this phase.
insights.quote: The Visser Labs 46 name index is up year to date 50%. Bitcoin is down 3.2%

insights.claim: Visser calls this the 'Micron moment': he expected Micron to double or triple and it went 14x on earnings growth, and he sees crypto/token volumes similarly surging from tokenization, stablecoin payments and AI agents, leaving wealth advisors in a difficult position within a year.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: People underestimate how fast token volumes will grow; get ahead now.
insights.quote: I thought Micron would double. I thought it might triple 14 times.

themes.theme: AI-crypto convergence in public markets and agentic indexing

insights.claim: Pompliano predicts that in 2027 public AI companies will rush into crypto and crypto companies into AI, making value accrual harder to judge; Coinbase skews crypto DNA and Robinhood brokerage/equities DNA.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Pick convergence plays by DNA mix; Sylvia pitched as only public AI+Bitcoin combo.
insights.quote: One of my predictions for 2027 is you're going to start to see an assault of public markets

insights.claim: Pompliano cautions that agentic custom indexing won't happen as fast as claimed because antiquated rules built for ETFs and mutual funds leave open whether agents or platforms need RIA-type registration, akin to unresolved DEX regulation; eToro, Robinhood, Coinbase, Public and Autopilot are all moving there.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Regulatory lag is the key timing risk for agentic trading products.
insights.quote: I do not think it will happen as fast as everyone claims it will.
